newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Newlywed Havel gives up smoking and drinking.
newsitem.headline: Newlywed Havel gives up smoking and drinking.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel said on Sunday he had given up smoking and drinking since surgeons removed a malignant tumour and half of his lung last month.
"Fate let me see it would be good to give up so I have given up," he said in his regular radio speech, a day after marrying for the second time.

"Not only have I become a non-smoker, I have even had to become a teetotaller. I hope that it will not be forever," he added in the regular Sunday broadcast, recorded soon after his marriage to Czech actress Dagmar Veskrnova, 43, on Saturday.
Havel's first wife Olga died of cancer last January aged 62.

"But I have always disliked militant non-smokers, I mean those ideological ones with a fanatic glimmer in the eye for whom their own fight is the same drug as a cigarette to a smoker...I have not become one of those," he added.

Havel, a heavy smoker for decades, left hospital late last month several weeks after an operation to remove a malignant tumour from his lungs. He contracted pneumonia soon afterwards and had to be connected to a respirator.
The 60-year-old former dissident playwright-turned-politician rejected oft-repeated suggestions that smoking had caused his illness.
"It was five or six neglected pneumonias I suffered from in jail (rather than smoking). The last I had was so serious they chose to release me for fear I might die," Havel said.
Havel, who became head of state after the peaceful overthrow of communist rule in 1989, spent several years in prison under their 40-year regime because of his dissident activities.
